subject: Privatelink/NAT egress & KMS/HSM keystore clarification for residency
messages:
From: Markus Hooper <mhooper@aurorahealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: security@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2027-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions: privatelink egress, KMS/HSM residency

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Aurora is working through the SIG/CAIQ and we need a few clarifications for the EU-only hosting requirement before we complete our internal security review. Can you confirm the following for Redwood Private deployments in eu-west-1 (Ireland)?

1) Network egress: If we connect via AWS PrivateLink into a customer-managed VPC, does any outbound traffic to other AWS regions or third-party services traverse Redwood-managed NAT or public internet egress? We need an affirmative that data paths do not leave EU without explicit customer-configured cross-region failover.

2) IP/endpoint allowlisting: Do you provide static IP ranges or endpoint DNS names for egress when PrivateLink is in use? We need guidance for our NSGs and firewall rules.

3) Keystore: Can KMS keys be customer-managed (bring-your-own key) and kept in our AWS KMS in eu-west-1, or does Redwood require any key material to be in Redwood-managed HSMs outside the region for certain features (e.g., managed snapshot encryption)? If HSM is used, is it FIPS 140-2/L4?

4) Audit & logs: Will audit logs (access, admin, and network flow logs) be retained in our account or sent to Redwood? What is the retention window and can we get a sample SOC2 artifact confirming log integrity controls?

5) Attachments: please attach the CAIQ/SIG responses you referenced and any network diagram for the PrivateLink flow.

We appreciate concise, point-by-point answers so our InfoSec team can close the questionnaire.

Best,
Markus
Director, Security Architecture
Aurora Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Hooper <mhooper@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: privatelink egress, KMS/HSM residency

Markus —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (security/compliance) and Irene (enterprise ops) to confirm a couple of specifics, but high-level answers below and I attached the CAIQ/SIG sheet and a PrivateLink diagram. I also attached our SOC 2 summary (redacted) and our KMS/HSM ops runbook.

Point-by-point:
1) Network egress: When you deploy Redwood Private inside your AWS account (customer-managed VPC) and front it with AWS PrivateLink, all inference request/response traffic remains in your VPC and the connected AZ/region unless you explicitly enable cross-region failover. Redwood does not route traffic via Redwood-managed NAT or public egress by default. Any optional telemetry forwarding (metrics/logs) can be configured to use a customer endpoint in-region.

2) IP/endpoint allowlisting: PrivateLink provides stable interface endpoint DNS names (com.amazonaws.vpce.<vpce-id>.service) — we provide the endpoint service name and recommended DNS entries in the diagram. There are no static public IPs for the interface endpoint; we recommend allowlisting the VPC endpoint service and the interface endpoint ENIs in your account. If you need a fixed egress IP for third-party vendors, we can publish a pattern for a customer-managed egress NAT in the runbook.

3) Keystore: BYOK is supported — you can supply and control keys in your AWS KMS in eu-west-1 for data-at-rest encryption. Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS keys and optional Redwood-managed HSM-backed keys. We do not require key material to leave the region. For customers requiring FIPS-certified HSMs, we offer integrations with FIPS-validated HSM services (customer or Redwood-managed) — details in the ops runbook.

4) Audit & logs: Audit logs (API access, admin actions, and connection logs) can be stored in your account (S3/CloudWatch/Logs) via an in-region sink. By default we can configure log exports to your S3 bucket in eu-west-1; retention and lifecycle policies are under your control. Attached is the SOC 2 summary and a redacted sample showing log integrity controls (hashing + rotation).

5) Attachments: attached CAIQ/SIG file and network diagram (see drive link below).

Next steps: if Aurora needs a written attestation we can sign, Karthik — can you prepare a short hosting attestation letter for EU-only residency and PrivateLink-only egress? Irene — can your team confirm the exact DNS endpoint and provide runbook text for the NAT option?

Happy to hop on a short technical call this week to walk through the diagram.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
https://redwood.com/solutions

Subject: Re: Questions: privatelink egress, KMS/HSM residency

Thanks Ben — that addresses most of the items. Two follow-ups from our InfoSec team:

• Cross-region failover: if we enable failover for DR, will Redwood require any temporary replication to a non-EU region during failover testing? We need explicit confirmation of data path behavior during a failover window.

• Token-level telemetry: does any telemetry/exported event include token-level input/output content (we strip PII before sending telemetry), or is telemetry limited to metadata (latency, model id, request size, success/failure)?

Also, please confirm whether the HSM options you mentioned are available in eu-west-1 with FIPS validation (or whether Redwood-managed HSMs are only in us regions today).

Cheers,
Markus

Markus —

Quick answers to the follow-ups and summary of what we attached/where to find the artifacts:

• Cross-region failover: By default, failover within Redwood Private is customer-controlled. If you opt into an automated cross-region failover policy, we will only replicate the minimal state necessary (model artifacts and KV caches) and will do so to a region you explicitly designate. We will not perform any replication to non-EU regions unless you configure a non-EU DR target. For failover testing we can provide a temporary, auditable window and describe the exact replication steps in the runbook.

• Telemetry contents: Telemetry exports contain metadata only (request ID, latency, model version, token counts, success/failure, error stacks). We do not include raw input/output tokens in telemetry exports by default. If a customer opts into content-level logging for debugging, that is configurable and must be explicitly enabled, and we strongly recommend doing so to a customer-controlled S3 bucket in-region with appropriate ACLs.

• HSM availability: Customer-managed HSM/KMS in eu-west-1 is fully supported for encryption-at-rest. Redwood-managed HSM-backed key stores (FIPS-validated) are available via partner integrations in eu-west-1 for customers who want Redwood to manage HSMs; note that full FIPS 140-2 L3/L4 attestation depends on the partner HSM provider and can be detailed per-customer. Karthik — I deferred a couple of HSM attestation specifics to you; can you confirm partner coverage in eu-west-1 and whether any Redwood-managed HSMs are colocated in EU today?
